title: Binary and ternary derived monoidal comparison data
statement:
Let $C,D$ be monoidal categories [def-sfb-monoidal-category], with tensors $\otimes$ and $\star$, associators $\alpha$ and $a$, and let $L:C\to D$ be a localization at a class $W$ containing identities, in the sense of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property]. Use $f;g=g\circ f$ for composition. Binary and ternary derived monoidal comparison data on $(L,\star,a)$ mean a natural transformation $q_{X,Y}:LX\star LY\to L(X\otimes Y)$ with the following properties.

For categories $A,B,H$, functors $J:A\to B$, $F:A\to H$, $R:B\to H$, and $e:R\circ J\Rightarrow F$, say that $(R,e)$ has the right Kan universal property along $J$ if for every $V:B\to H$ the map
$$\operatorname{Nat}(V,R)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Nat}(V\circ J,F),\qquad t\longmapsto(tJ);e$$
is a bijection. Here $\operatorname{Nat}$ denotes families of morphisms commuting with every arrow, and the categories of tuples have componentwise arrows. All functor categories are formed in a common sufficiently large universe.

Require this property for $J=L\times L$, $R(U,V)=U\star V$, $F(X,Y)=L(X\otimes Y)$, $e=q$. Also require it for $J=L\times L\times L$ and both pairs
$$R_l(U,V,Z)=(U\star V)\star Z,\quad F_l(X,Y,Z)=L((X\otimes Y)\otimes Z),\quad e_l=q^l,$$
$$R_r(U,V,Z)=U\star(V\star Z),\quad F_r(X,Y,Z)=L(X\otimes(Y\otimes Z)),\quad e_r=q^r,$$
where
$$q^l_{X,Y,Z}=(q_{X,Y}\star1_{LZ});q_{X\otimes Y,Z},\qquad q^r_{X,Y,Z}=(1_{LX}\star q_{Y,Z});q_{X,Y\otimes Z}.$$
Finally require the associator comparison equation
$$a_{LX,LY,LZ};q^r_{X,Y,Z}=q^l_{X,Y,Z};L(\alpha_{X,Y,Z}).$$
The associator symbols in this equation denote the forward maps of their isomorphisms. These are conditions on specified tensor, associator and comparison data.

Type check: q^l=(q⋆1);q goes (LX⋆LY)⋆LZ→L((X⊗Y)⊗Z), q^r=(1⋆q);q goes LX⋆(LY⋆LZ)→L(X⊗(Y⊗Z)), and both sides of a;q^r=q^l;Lα run from (LX⋆LY)⋆LZ to L(X⊗(Y⊗Z)). The Kan property t↦(tJ);e is the right-Kan (left-derived counit) direction, matching Mathlib KanExtension/Basic.lean:74-113 (homEquivOfIsRightKanExtension). It also matches the project Lean FromJoel/.../Monoidal/Derived.lean: counit₁₂_app and counit₂₃_app give q^l and q^r, HasDerivedMonoidalCategory at 143-156 gives the binary and ternary conditions (its unit and quaternary conditions are deliberately left out), and associator_hom_fac_app_app_app at 175-183 is exactly the item's equation. The ternary Kan property of q^r determines a uniquely, which covers the parent citer's claim that a is the induced associator.
